supplement.where: External supplementary dataset mentioned on p. 10, Section 3.7; supplementary XLSX files named in Appendix G, pp. 56-58, with no download URL. In contrast, Appendices A-H themselves are embedded in this PDF (pp. 26-64). The false flag refers to the external dataset/spreadsheets, not the embedded appendices.
supplement.holds: External dataset: representative coded exemplars (p. 10). External XLSX files: complete marginal means and CR2 simple contrasts at low/high BDI, including SI_z_gain_EMMs_BDI_minus.xlsx, SI_z_gain_EMMs_BDI_plus.xlsx and SI_z_gain_CR2_BDI_CR2.xlsx for performance gain (pp. 56 and 58). The PDF already contains the main creative-task coefficients and SEs in Table 28, EMMs in Table 29, and BDI-adjusted variants in Tables 31-32 (pp. 52-55). Dimension-specific originality, elaboration and coherence effects are not printed; the document does not establish whether those are in the external files.

paper_design_summary: An online experiment analyzed 905 Prolific participants across analytical, ethical and creative tasks in randomly assigned human-only or hybrid triads with supportive, contrarian or mixed AI teammates (pp. 2-6). Participants completed the task individually before and after group discussion; blinded researchers rated individual movie plots for originality, elaboration and coherence, supporting an immediate after-AI creativity outcome (pp. 5-6 and 9-11). A separate pilot with 15 people assessed AI humanness and supplied no creative-output outcome (p. 8).

studies.label: Main online experiment: analytical, ethical and creative tasks; creative-writing outcomes coded

assignment.what_was_assigned: Triads were randomly assigned to human-only or hybrid teams differing in AI persona and number of AI teammates (p. 2, Introduction). Section 3.2 describes participants randomly assigned to groups and group conditions within each task. Task and team condition vary between groups; individual performance is measured before and after discussion. The randomization algorithm and allocation counts before exclusions are not stated.
assignment.quote: Triads were randomly assigned to human-only teams or to groups that included one or two AI agents programmed with distinct personas, supportive or contrarian.

participants.exclusions: 1,047 participants initially entered, not an explicitly reported randomized count. Exclusions: failed attention check n = 36; inadequate discussion engagement n = 67 (fewer than five messages and average message length below 20 characters); incomplete post-task survey n = 20; individual task mismatched to discussion task n = 19. Final primary analysis: 905 people in 572 groups (pp. 3-4, Section 3.1). Identifier mismatches excluded another 34 people only from BDI analyses, leaving 871; they remained in other analyses (p. 4, Section 3.1). Creative-task cell counts are printed separately in Table 2; no total for that task is explicitly printed, so none is calculated here.
participants.who: English-fluent adult Prolific participants, recruited between 21 August 2025 and 20 September 2025. Stated eligibility age range is 18-65; Table 1 nevertheless includes a 65+ category. The 905-person count describes the entire main experiment, not just the creative-writing task (pp. 3-4, Section 3.1 and Table 1).
participants.country: Countries not stated individually. Table 1 reports North America/Central America, South America, Europe, Africa, Asia and Australia (p. 4).
participants.quote: After applying these exclusions, the final analytic sample for the primary analyses comprised 𝑁= 905 participants, clustered within 572 three-person groups.
participants.locator: pp. 3-4, Section 3.1 and Table 1; p. 6, Table 2

ai_tool.name_model: Conversational generative-AI agents; underlying model, provider and version not stated.
ai_tool.how_used: Undisclosed AI teammates participated in synchronous group chat using supportive or contrarian system prompts, with a mixed-persona configuration when two agents were present. They contributed to the discussion under a scheduling protocol and were prohibited from revealing their artificial identity. Participants then repeated the task individually. This is an AI teammate intervention, not an AI-versus-human output benchmark (pp. 5-8, Sections 3.2-3.5; pp. 29-31, Appendix B).

task.description: The eligible task is to develop an original feature-film plot with AGI central to the story, specifying characters, setting, key events and resolution (p. 7, Section 3.3; p. 28, Appendix A.3). Participants produce an individual baseline, discuss the task with their assigned teammates, then repeat it individually (pp. 5-6). The same experiment also includes survival ranking and autonomous-vehicle ethical reasoning; these are not separate independent studies and their performance results are outside the creative-output extraction.
task.duration: Group discussion: 10 minutes. Individual baseline and post-task durations not stated (p. 5, Section 3.2; p. 6, Figure 2).

outcomes.name: Individual creative-writing performance gain (composite rubric score, post-task minus baseline)
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Movie-plot submissions were scored for originality, elaboration and coherence on five-point rubrics by two independent researchers trained in education and psychology, blinded to condition; final ratings average the two raters (pp. 9-10, Section 3.7; p. 33, Table 9). Table 6 reports a creative-writing total score as well as each dimension (p. 11). The analyzed performance outcome is the standardized post-task-minus-baseline gain (p. 11, Section 3.9; pp. 51-53, Appendix F, Tables 28-29). Exact aggregation of dimensions and the standardization denominator are not specified. A mixed-effects model uses a group random intercept; CR2 standard errors cluster by group with Satterthwaite degrees of freedom and Holm correction (pp. 12-13, Section 3.11). The model uses the full cross-task dataset, with Creative/H3 as reference; the condition coefficients are creative-task contrasts, not pooled effects across tasks. BDI-adjusted analyses (pp. 54-55, Tables 31-32) and BDI moderation (pp. 56-58, Appendix G) are robustness variants of this same outcome. Table 29 EMM standard errors are kept distinct from Table 28 CR2 contrast standard errors.
outcomes.delay: Same-session individual Phase C follows the group discussion; the same task is repeated individually (p. 5, Section 3.2; p. 6, Figure 2). No delayed session is reported.

Table 29 standardized gain EMMs: H2_S 0.212 (SE 0.133, 95% CI [-0.049, 0.472], df 519) versus H3 -0.124 (SE 0.108, 95% CI [-0.336, 0.089], df 210). These are coefficients and marginal means of the standardized gain outcome, not raw post-test means or a reported Cohen's d. Table 2 analyzed people: H2_S n = 57, H3 n = 90.

outcomes.name: Originality of individual movie plot
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Novelty, surprise and departure from conventional science-fiction plots. This dimension was scored on individual pre- and post-discussion submissions using a five-point rubric (pp. 9-10, Section 3.7; p. 33, Table 9); both pre and post dimensions appear in the reliability table (p. 11, Table 6). Ratings were averaged across two independent, condition-blinded researchers with training in education and psychology. The post-discussion submission is unassisted Phase C (pp. 5-6, Section 3.2 and Figure 2). The dimension contributes to the composite performance outcome, but separate arm means, SDs and treatment effects for this dimension are not reported in the PDF. Reliability coefficients are not treatment effects; no direction is inferred from the composite.
outcomes.delay: Same-session individual post-discussion task; no later follow-up reported (pp. 5-6, Section 3.2 and Figure 2).

eligibility.reason: The main study explicitly randomizes triads to human-only or AI-teammate conditions (p. 2, Introduction; pp. 4-6, Section 3.2). The final main-study analytic sample is 905 people (p. 4, Section 3.1), and the creative-writing control alone contains 90 analyzed people, with additional people in each AI arm (p. 6, Table 2); thus the eligible task also exceeds the threshold without relying on ratings or group counts. Individual movie plots receive external rubric scores for originality, elaboration and coherence (pp. 9-11, Sections 3.7 and 3.9; p. 33, Table 9). The post-discussion individual task is after_ai (pp. 5-6), with printed treatment coefficients and SEs (p. 52, Table 28). Human teammates are the active comparator. The separate humanness pilot does not qualify: no randomized AI comparison or scored creative output is reported (p. 8).

one_line_finding: After the AI-teammate discussion, creative-writing gains showed no clear difference from human-only teams: the supportive one-AI contrast was 0.336 standardized gain units (CR2 SE 0.184, p = .074, Holm p = 1.00), and every other creative-task AI-versus-human-team contrast also had Holm p = 1.00 (p. 52, Table 28).
open_questions: The underlying generative model, provider and version are not specified in Sections 3.4-3.5 or Appendix B (pp. 7-8 and 29-31).
The PDF names external XLSX moderation outputs and a supplementary dataset but supplies no access URL (p. 10 and pp. 56-58). Their contents were not available for this extraction.

The exact combination of creative-writing dimensions into the total and the denominator used to standardize performance gain are not specified (p. 11, Section 3.9; pp. 51-53, Appendix F). Raw arm means/SDs and dimension-specific treatment effects are not printed.

BDI is defined as Balanced Detection Index in the main methods, but Appendix G calls it baseline depressive symptoms (p. 10, Section 3.8 versus p. 56). This inconsistency needs author clarification for moderator interpretation; the primary extracted contrasts do not adjust for BDI.
notes: Read the entire markdown conversion, including all appendices, and checked cited design/count/rubric/result pages with PyMuPDF. Page locators are one-based PDF pages. The file contains 64 pages, although footers say of 65; no extra page was assumed. One main experiment is retained as one study across its task cells, and the explicitly independent pilot is a second study. The arms array lists task-by-condition cells to preserve the printed people counts without deriving pooled arm totals. The total n_analyzed of 905 is for all tasks, not the creative task alone. Table 2 is described as assigned counts in prose, but its cells represent the final analytic sample; pre-exclusion randomized counts are therefore null. The three component scores are listed because they were scored on output, with empty contrasts because component-specific treatment statistics are not supplied. Baseline component ratings and BDI robustness analyses are not counted as additional outcomes. Group discussion quality and its idea-generation/sharing, engagement and progression/synthesis dimensions assess interaction processes from chat transcripts (pp. 11-12, Section 3.9; p. 33, Table 8); they are not coded here as creativity of the individual movie plots or diversity across people. Self-reported satisfaction/safety, AI detection, AI linguistic persona checks and humanness ratings are also outside the three atlas questions. The analytical survival-ranking and ethical-reasoning scores are not creative-output measures. No across_people measure is reported. AI-versus-H3 contrasts use ai_vs_active because AI teammates replace human collaborators, and the human-only arms use other_aid for human partners. No effect sizes or unprinted sample totals were calculated. No other screening form was consulted.
